subject: Simsem in R: Power analysis estimation with X dichotomous but W continous

messages.author: 6d37bd3b53d6200d
messages.subject: Simsem in R: Power analysis estimation with X dichotomous but W continous
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to run a power analysis estimation for a moderated mediation model, similar to that describe in Table 4 of this paper/tutorial:  

Donnelly, S., Jorgensen, T. D., & Rudolph, C. W. (2021). Power Analysis for Conditional Indirect Effects: A Tutorial for Conducting Monte Carlo Simulations with Categorical Exogenous Variables.

However, the syntax described in Table 4 (and reported slighly adjusted below) considers both X and W (the moderator) as dichotomous. 

How can I adapt the script below if only X is dichotomous (and M, Y and W are continuous variables)?

Thank you in advance,

Mattia


      


N.per.group <- 50 # balanced group sample sizes
designMatrix <- expand.grid(X = 1:0, W = 1:0)
designMatrix$XW <- designMatrix$X * designMatrix$W # interaction
exoData <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:N.per.group, function(i) designMatrix))
a.w0 <-1.03 #effectofXonMwhenmoderator(W)==0
a.mod <- -.8 # how much “a” path is moderated by W (i.e., interaction)
b.w0 <-.25#effectofMonYwhenmoderator(W)==0
b.mod <- 0 # no moderating effect on “b” path
c.w0 <-.31#effectofXonYwhenmoderator(W)==0
c.mod <- 0 # no moderating effect on “c” path
w.M <- .15 # simple effect of moderator (W) on M when X == 0
w.Y <- -.2 # simple effect of moderator (W) on Y when X == 0
kappa.free <- kappa.pop <- matrix(NA, # estimate all effects
                                  nrow = 2, # 2 outcomes (M and Y)
                                  ncol = 3, # dummy coded X, W, XW dimnames = list(c(“M”,”Y”),
                                  dimnames = list(c('M','Y'), names(exoData)))  
kappa.free['M','X'] <- 'a.w0' # label free parameters
kappa.free['M','W'] <- 'w.M' # (to define indirect effects)
kappa.free['M','XW'] <- 'a.mod'
kappa.free['Y','X'] <- 'c.w0'
kappa.free['Y','W'] <- 'w.Y'
kappa.free['Y','XW'] <- 0 # fixed to 0; label “c.mod” to free
kappa.pop['M','X']  <- a.w0
kappa.pop['M','W']  <- w.M
kappa.pop['M','XW'] <- a.mod
kappa.pop['Y','X']  <- c.w0
kappa.pop['Y','W']  <- w.Y
kappa.pop['Y','XW'] <- c.mod
             
exoPaths <- bind(free = kappa.free, popParam = kappa.pop)
beta.free <- beta.pop <- matrix(0, nrow = 3, ncol = 1,dimnames = list(c('M','Y','W'), 'X'))
beta.free['Y', 'M'] <- 'b'
beta.pop['Y', 'M'] <- b.w0
endoPaths <- bind(free = beta.free, popParam = beta.pop)
residCor <- binds(free = diag(as.numeric(NA), 2), popParam = diag(2)) ##### che number to 3 and 1
userParams <- ' ## conditional indirect effects
ind.w0   := a.w0 * b
ind.w1 := (a.w0 + a.mod) * b
## Test H0: equivalent indirect effects across W
ind.diff := a.mod * b
 ## or equivalently:
# ind.diff := ind.w1 – ind.w0 '
modMed1 <- model.path(BE = endoPaths, RPS = residCor, KA = exoPaths, con = userParams, indLab = rownames(kappa.free),covLab = colnames(kappa.free))
rejectMCCI <- function(object) {  
  CIs <- semTools::monteCarloCI(object)
  apply(CIs, 1, function(CI) 0 < CI['ci.lower'] | 0 > CI['ci.upper']) }
sim1 <- sim(nRep = 1000, model = modMed1, covData = exoData,n = nrow(exoData), seed = 777,
            outfun = rejectMCCI, meanstructure = FALSE) # pass this argument to lavaan
summaryParam(sim1, matchParam = TRUE, digits = 3)
testMCCI <- do.call(rbind, getExtraOutput(sim1))
colMeans(testMCCI) # empirical estimate of power for Monte Carlo CIs

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Simsem in R: Power analysis estimation with X dichotomous but W continous
parts: How can I adapt the script below if only X is dichotomous (and M, Y and W are continuous variables)?

You can generate any fixed exogenous data you want.  How do you want W to be distributed?  Is W supposed to represent something like age, which would be uniformly distributed in your sampling frame / population of interest (e.g., kids between 7 and 10 years old)?

designMatrix <- expand.grid(X = 1:0, W = 7:10)

It can get more complicated, depending on what scenario you want to simulate.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Simsem in R: Power analysis estimation with X dichotomous but W continous
parts: I would like it to be a normal distributed variable (just like M and Y). Is this possible?

Sure.  Do you want it to be homoskedastic and orthogonal to X?  If so, you can center/scale W within each X group, so X and W are uncorrelated.

N.per.group <- 50
exoData <- data.frame(X = rep(0:1, each = N.per.group))
exoData$W <- rnorm(N.per.group*2)
exoData$W[exoData$X == 0] <- scale(exoData$W[exoData$X == 0])[,1]
exoData$W[exoData$X == 1] <- scale(exoData$W[exoData$X == 1])[,1]
round(cor(exoData), 10)
aggregate(W ~ X, data = exoData, FUN = sd)
Are there other parts in the script that require any further adjustment?

If you are getting that drawParam() error, perhaps you need to specify standardized parameters more carefully.  The tutorial shows how to use the simsem::find*() functions to find the residual variance that would make the total variance 1.  Making sure your explained variance is not > 1 can prevent the drawParam() error.
How can I cite your tutorial paper?

You can use the reference you put in your OP, but add the DOI from the PsyArXiv page.

https://psyarxiv.com/35768/

It is still under review, but the last round was pretty light, so we are hoping our revision will be accepted soon.  Feel free to email me privately when you are ready to submit your paper, and I will let you know if there is an updated DOI and journal you can add.

Thanks,

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
